doc.title: Rudy Van Gelder — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Sherwood, big bands and sound concept
title: Acetate playbacks and the sound-wave label artist
summary: He made acetate playbacks with a printed label designed by a newspaper artist friend.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: And Eddie Byrd, remember him? He was on some of your earliest records in ’53.

You mean about Debut. Yeah I used to make playbacks, acetate playbacks, and I had a bunch of labels I used to stick on so you knew what the label was, what the record was. I had a cart of them out here from the printer. Oh there is the house…jeez.
Tell us what it was like.
A friend of mine knew and artist.
And that’s a sound wave huh?

Yeah he was pretty famous and he drew for the newspapers. If I mentioned the name you would know who he was. He lives in Connecticut, or did live in Connecticut. I cant remember. So he asked to design the label for me, and he did. That’s the one with that little one sound wave line. Oh, here! So he did that and I used to put that on all of my playbacks. An amateur would come in and record and then hand him a disc and that was the end of it.
